issues_found.issue: The engineer's D1 made bots fire real c.spawnProjectile shots, but _onProjectileHit now applies those hits via `this._request({ type: 'hit', target: target.id, damage: item.damage })` with NO fromBotId. The old c.onHit callback passed `b.netId` as the second arg; the new path drops it. Consequences: (1) OFFLINE solo/2p-vs-bots: _request → sim.request('local', evt), so the bot's hit resolves with shooter = local player. Because match.js assigns teams by join order (local player = blue, i=0) and a red bot's shot on the blue player is now a same-team pair, _hit() returns early on `target.team === shooter.team` — BOT PROJECTILES DO ZERO DAMAGE TO THE HUMAN IN SOLO PLAY. (2) Bot-vs-bot downs instead increment the human's `kills` (shooter.kills++ on local). (3) ONLINE (host): _request → net.event(evt) instead of net.botEvent(item.owner, evt), so the server credits the kill to the host and validates against the wrong author.
issues_found.suggestion: In the bot-owned branch pass item.owner as the second arg, exactly like the removed callback did: `this._request({ type: 'hit', target: target.id, damage: item.damage }, item.owner);` (guard it to the `ownerIsBot` case). This yields offline sim.request(item.owner, …) and online net.botEvent(item.owner, …), restoring correct attribution and unblocking bot damage to the player. One-line fix.

issues_found.issue: ownerIsBot is true on EVERY client (bots live in this.bots everywhere). If bot projectiles are replicated to clients (not host-only), each client that simulates a bot projectile independently calls _request for the same hit, which could apply/emit the down multiple times and fire multiple net.events.
issues_found.suggestion: Confirm bot projectiles are spawned/owned only on the host. On non-host clients, treat bot-owned projectiles like remote-human shots (draw only, owner reports), or have the server reconcile duplicate hit events. Requires a real 2+ client networked playtest to confirm.
